audits.title: An Audit of Documentation Relating to a Decision-Making Capacity to Consent to Admission to the Peter Bruff Mental Health Assessment Unit
audits.standard: NICE NG108 (2018) recommendations 1.4: 100% of admitted patients should have MCA completed during admission clerking
audits.setting: Peter Bruff Mental Health Assessment Unit

cycle1.result: MCA completed with capacity at clerking and review in 85%; lacked capacity at clerking 3%; capacity at admission but not at review 5%; MCA not completed or unavailable in 7%

audits.other_findings: Discrepancy between clerking and later reviews suggests further training needed.
audits.citation: Zinchenko O, Sivakanthan S, Rai Y, Shoka A. An Audit of Documentation Relating to a Decision-Making Capacity to Consent to Admission to the Peter Bruff Mental Health Assessment Unit. BJPsych Open. 2023;9(S1):S146-S147. doi:10.1192/bjo.2023.398.

audits.title: Improving the Quality, Accuracy and Consistency of Capacity Assessments Across Inpatient Psychiatric Wards at the Harbour (FC Locality)
audits.standard: Mental Capacity Act (2005), MCA Code of Practice, Trust MCA policy and NICE NG97; target ≥80% of assessments meeting all components
audits.setting: The Harbour, 154-bed mental health hospital (general adult, older adult, dementia and PICU wards)

cycle1.result: Decision and time specificity 100%; diagnostic test 77.5%; functional components 70% each; clinical reasoning 60%; correct template use 67.5%; decision-specific framing 60%; outcome stated 92.5%.

audits.intervention: 30-minute targeted teaching for resident doctors on MCA principles and the capacity template, reinforced through MDT discussions, handovers and optional quick-reference guidance.

cycle2.result: Diagnostic test 95%; understand 92.5%, retain 90%, use/weigh 90%, communicate 100%; clinical reasoning, template use and decision-specific framing 92.5%; outcome 97.5%.

audits.citation: Hosein C. Improving the Quality, Accuracy and Consistency of Capacity Assessments Across Inpatient Psychiatric Wards at the Harbour (FC Locality). BJPsych Open. 2026;12(S1):S158-S159. doi:10.1192/bjo.2026.11394.

audits.title: Mental Capacity Assessments on Admission: An Audit
audits.standard: Trust Inpatient Admissions SOP: capacity to consent to treatment assessed within 24 hours of admission; MCA Code of Practice (decision-specific, four-part functional test, least restrictive, best interests)
audits.setting: Beech Unit, Torbay, Devon Partnership Trust (inpatient)

cycle1.result: Capacity assessment within 24 hours 100%; MCA template completed in 90% (half within timeframe); decision documented 90%; functional test 90%; least restrictive and best interests 53%

audits.other_findings: Recommended using the Trust standardised MCA template and guidance for clerking doctors.
audits.citation: Ahmed F, Forbes C. Mental Capacity Assessments on Admission: An Audit. BJPsych Open. 2026;12(S1):S274-S275. doi:10.1192/bjo.2026.11564.

audits.title: A Clinical Audit to Improve Documentation of Mental Capacity Assessments in Acute Hospital Liaison Teams
audits.standard: 100% documentation of capacity assessment; minimum Grade 2 detail for all four functional stages
audits.setting: Chesterfield Mental Health Liaison Team, acute hospital, Derbyshire Healthcare Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: Broad capacity assessment recorded in 90%; specific decision documented in 37%; no evidence (Grade 0) for Understanding and Communicating in 50%, and for Weighing-up in 40%.

audits.intervention: Recommended mandatory MCA forms in the core electronic assessment template
audits.citation: Williams O, Azam B. A Clinical Audit to Improve Documentation of Mental Capacity Assessments in Acute Hospital Liaison Teams. BJPsych Open. 2026;12(S1):S352-S353. doi:10.1192/bjo.2026.11753.

audits.title: Improving recording of capacity to consent and explanation of medication side effects in a psychiatric service for people with learning disability: audit findings.
audits.standard: Recording of capacity to consent to treatment and documentation of side-effect explanation

cycle1.result: Capacity recorded in 30% of case notes.

audits.intervention: Rubber stamp in case notes introduced in 2008 as a visual prompt

cycle2.result: Capacity recorded in 51% (P = 0.000006); capacity more likely recorded when stamp present (OR 13.5, p < 0.0001).

audits.other_findings: Three audit cycles 2007-2009 of 26 random notes each; recording of side-effect discussion was consistently higher and changed little.
audits.citation: Roy A, Jain S, Roy A, Ward F, Richings C, Martin M, et al.. Improving recording of capacity to consent and explanation of medication side effects in a psychiatric service for people with learning disability: audit findings. J Intellect Disabil. 2011;15(2):85-92. doi:10.1177/1744629511410826. PMID: 21750211.

audits.title: Capacity in vacuo: an audit of decision-making capacity assessments in a liaison psychiatry service.
audits.standard: Legal criteria of the Mental Capacity Act 2005 (gold-standard documentation)
audits.setting: Liaison psychiatry service, South London and Maudsley NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: 21 capacity assessments (6.9% of referrals); none met the gold standard.

audits.intervention: Legally focused educational intervention to staff.

cycle2.result: Month 16 (during intervention): 27 assessments (9.7%), 2 met gold standard; month 21: 24 assessments (6.6%), none met gold standard.

audits.other_findings: No effect of the educational intervention was shown; severity of consequences (OR 24.4) and not agreeing to the intervention (OR 21.8) predicted lacking capacity.
audits.citation: Spencer BW, Wilson G, Okon-Rocha E, Owen GS, Wilson Jones C. Capacity in vacuo: an audit of decision-making capacity assessments in a liaison psychiatry service. BJPsych Bull. 2017;41(1):7-11. doi:10.1192/pb.bp.115.052613. PMID: 28184310.

audits.title: Audit of Mental Capacity Assessment by Primary Care Physicians Versus Consultation-liaison Psychiatrists.
audits.setting: In-patients referred to consultation-liaison psychiatry, Singapore General Hospital

cycle1.result: Assessments by primary care physicians were suboptimal; consultation-liaison psychiatrists documented mental capacity in 93.7% and psychiatric diagnosis in 88.9%.

audits.other_findings: Patient wishes and beliefs documented in 19.0%, lasting power of attorney or deputy in 6.3% and advance care planning in 0%.
audits.citation: Chan CY, Yong SW, Mhaisalkar AS, Sin GL, Poon SH, Tan SM. Audit of Mental Capacity Assessment by Primary Care Physicians Versus Consultation-liaison Psychiatrists. East Asian Arch Psychiatry. 2018;28(3):95-100. doi:10.12809/eaap1752. PMID: 30146497.
